abstract: Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76791-y Nonflammable electrolytes are key to safe potassium-ion batteries but suffer from poor electrode compatibility. Here, authors design a phosphate molecule with long side-chains enabling strong chelation and anion-reinforced solvation, leading to high electrode compatibility.

title: Electrochemical Modeling of LiFePO4 Cathodes: Role of Particle Size Distribution and Variable Solid Phase Diffusion Coefficient
authors: Mohamed Atwair, Hunter A McRay, Paul Coman, Golareh Jalilvand and Ralph E White
abstract: This study presents a simplified yet physically robust electrochemical model for <mark>lithium</mark> iron phosphate (LiFePO4 or LFP) cathodes, aimed at improving the accuracy of voltage prediction across various C-rates without relying on complex phase-transition modeling. The model is developed within a pseudo-two-dimensional (P2D) framework and incorporates key features such as variable solid-state diffusivity (VSSD) and particle size distribution (PSD).
